articles.title: Michael Jordan’s legacy keeps growing 23 years after retirement as his sneaker empire reaches No. 41
articles.standfirst: The No. 23 walked off an NBA court for the final time in 2003, but the story attached to his name never really stopped moving
articles.summary: The No. 23 walked off an NBA court for the final time in 2003, but the story attached to his name never really stopped moving
articles.body:
F or Michael Jordan, numbers have always meant something. Six championships. Five MVP awards. Ten scoring titles. And, above all of them, 23 the number that became so inseparable from the man that generations of kids wanted it on their backs simply because he had worn it first.

On April 16, 2003, Jordan walked onto an NBA court for the final time. He was 40 years old, wearing a Washington Wizards uniform instead of Chicago red, when Philadelphia intentionally fouled him late in the game so he could score the final two points of his career from the free-throw line. The crowd rose for him, and eventually Jordan disappeared toward the locker room. Basketball's No. 23 was finally done.

Twenty-three years later a coincidence almost too perfect for Michael Jordan another number has arrived. Jordan Brand has officially unveiled the Air Jordan 41 , the 41st chapter of a sneaker story that began when Jordan was a 21-year-old rookie and Nike took an enormous gamble on a young guard from North Carolina.

The 41 doesn't represent Jordan's age, championships or another jersey number. It is simply the 41st numbered Air Jordan. Yet reaching it says something remarkable: the shoes kept going long after the player stopped.

It started with a shoe that wasn't supposed to become this

Before there could be an Air Jordan 41, there had to be an Air Jordan 1.

Jordan's relationship with Nike began during his rookie season in 1984, and the first Air Jordan arrived commercially in 1985 . The black-and-red story surrounding those early shoes became sneaker mythology: the NBA objected to footwear that violated its uniform rules, and Nike transformed that controversy into marketing gold.

The famous tale that Jordan was fined $5,000 every time he wore the AJ1 in an NBA game isn't quite accurate. Nike itself now acknowledges that the shoe at the center of the original dispute was a black-and-red Nike Air Ship worn in the 1984 preseason. But the legend helped make the Air Jordan feel rebellious before sneaker culture even had a name.

And then something much bigger happened. People didn't only want to watch Michael Jordan. They wanted to wear Michael Jordan.

The Air Jordan 3 arrived in 1988 with Tinker Hatfield's design, elephant print and the Jumpman imagery that would eventually become recognizable far beyond basketball. The Air Jordan 4 became attached forever to “The Shot” over Craig Ehlo in the 1989 playoffs.

The Air Jordan 11 became one of the defining shoes of Jordan's return from baseball and later gained another life through Space Jam. The black-and-red Air Jordan 12 became inseparable from the legendary 1997 “Flu Game.” And the Air Jordan 13 accompanied Jordan into the final championship run of The Last Dance .

Some Jordans have become more valuable than houses

Perhaps the strangest proof of what Jordan created is what people are now willing to pay for shoes he actually wore.

A pair of Air Jordan 13s worn by Jordan during Game 2 of the 1998 NBA Finals sold for $2.2 million in 2023. Then came something even more extraordinary: the “Dynasty Collection,” consisting of six individual sneakers Jordan wore in the championship-clinching games of all six Bulls title runs. The collection sold for $8 million in 2024. They weren't even six complete pairs. They were six individual shoes.

There have been even stranger relics. A pair of Air Jordan 1s connected to a 1985 exhibition in Italy was sold with a piece of shattered backboard glass reportedly still embedded in the sole, a souvenir from the night Jordan dunked hard enough to break the glass.

Another pair associated with the game in which he fractured his left foot in 1985 sold for more than $400,000. Shoes once designed to be destroyed on a basketball court eventually became artifacts people handle like paintings.

That transformation has made Jordan extraordinarily wealthy, but the size of the business is perhaps more impressive than any estimate of his personal royalties. Nike reported $7.034 billion in Jordan Brand revenue during fiscal 2026 alone.

Forty years after the first Air Jordan, this is no nostalgic side business surviving on old photographs. It remains a multibillion-dollar global brand.

At 63, Michael Jordan is still influencing the shoe

That may be the most surprising part of the Air Jordan 41.

Jordan isn't merely an old photograph used to sell it. At 63, he was among the athletes whose feedback informed its development . Jordan Brand describes the AJ41 as lighter and more responsive, built around a first-of-its-kind 3D nano mesh upper, full-length ZoomX foam, Zoom Strobel cushioning and additional Air Zoom. The first colorways are inspired by gemstones, with each intended to represent qualities such as strength, courage, passion and creativity.

The first version is appropriately called “Ruby.” It arrives dressed in the red that has followed Jordan through so much of his life, and Nike has priced it at $205. Look closely and there is even another tiny reminder of the man behind it: the official color description includes “Infrared 23.” Forty-one shoes later, 23 is still there.

And Jordan himself hasn't exactly disappeared. He co-owns 23XI Racing even the NASCAR team's name combines his 23 with Denny Hamlin's 11 and just days before the AJ41 unveiling, Jordan visited the team's Airspeed headquarters to speak with its drivers and personnel ahead of NASCAR's postseason.

Meanwhile, another chapter of his brief return to NBA television appears to be closing: a report on August 27 said Jordan is not expected to return to NBC's NBA coverage after one season as a special contributor. Even at 63, his relationship with competition seems difficult to completely leave behind.

Maybe that's why the Air Jordan 41 feels different when viewed through the entire story.

A young Michael Jordan once put on the first shoes carrying his name without knowing whether there would ever be a second pair, much less a 41st model. He played his final NBA game on April 16, 2003, and left the floor with 32,292 career points, six rings and a number 23 already immortal.

Now, 23 years later, the player is long retired, but the footsteps haven't stopped.

Michael Jordan wore No. 23. His shoes have now reached No. 41. And somewhere between those two numbers lies one of the rarest achievements in sports: a career that ended, and a legacy that simply refused to.

articles.title: Kevin Durant’s AI jackpot may be the greatest athlete investment ever
articles.standfirst: The return could exceed what Durant is earning this season as an NBA player
articles.summary: The return could exceed what Durant is earning this season as an NBA player
articles.body:
K evin Durant has spent nearly two decades making defenders look helpless on the basketball court. But his latest victory may be even more impressive than anything he has accomplished in the NBA.

According to i nvestor and entrepreneur Joe Pompliano, Durant's early investment in artificial intelligence company Hugging Face has reportedly turned a combined $250,000 investment into a payout exceeding $60 million following Nvidia's acquisition of the company for $12.9 billion.

If the estimates are accurate, the transaction would rank among the most successful investments ever made by a professional athlete.

And perhaps most remarkably, the return could exceed what Durant is earning this season as an NBA player.

A massive return on a small initial bet

Pompliano revealed on social media that Durant and longtime business partner Rich Kleiman participated in Hugging Face's seed and Series A fundraising rounds through their investment platform, 35V. According to Pompliano, Durant invested $100,000 during the company's seed round and another $150,000 during its Series A financing.

Years later, that relatively modest $250,000 commitment appears to have generated a return worth more than $60 million. "Kevin Durant and his business partner, Rich Kleiman, invested in Hugging Face's seed & Series A fundraising rounds," Pompliano wrote. "And it just happens that tech giant Nvidia just acquired the company for $12.9 billion."

He added that the investment likely generated a profit that surpassed Durant's on-court earnings for the current season. For most investors, a return of that magnitude would represent a once-in-a-lifetime outcome. For Durant, it is another example of how aggressively he has approached business opportunities away from basketball..

More than an NBA superstar

Durant remains one of the highest-paid athletes in the world. The future Hall of Famer is currently playing under a two-year, $90 million contract extension and is set to earn nearly $44 million during the 2026-27 campaign. Combined with his lifetime Nike agreement and previous contracts, Durant has already surpassed $500 million in career NBA earnings.

Unlike many athletes who rely primarily on endorsement deals, Durant has increasingly positioned himself as a venture capitalist. Alongside Kleiman, he has built 35V into one of the most active athlete-led investment firms in sports.

The company has invested across technology, media, sports, and consumer brands, focusing on early-stage opportunities with significant growth potential. The Hugging Face investment appears to be one of the firm's biggest successes to date.

articles.title: The heartbreaking situation that Kobe Bryant's sister goes through every year on her daughter's birthday
articles.standfirst: Shaya Bryant reveals why her daughter’s birthday is also one of the hardest days of the year
articles.summary: Shaya Bryant reveals why her daughter’s birthday is also one of the hardest days of the year
articles.body:
August 23 is a date filled with emotions that are difficult to separate in Shaya Bryant’s world. It’s the birthday of her daughter, Autumn , but it’s also the birthday of her younger brother, Kobe Bryant.

Since Kobe’s death in 2020, what should be a joyful family occasion has also become a painful annual reminder of the NBA legend she lost.

Shaya recently opened up about the complicated emotions surrounding the date while appearing on the Born To The Game podcast. She described August 23 as both “a beauty and a curse,” explaining how public celebrations of Kobe’s life can bring comfort while also reopening the wounds of grief.

Kobe was born on August 23, 1978, and Autumn was born on the same date in 2008. The coincidence was especially remarkable because Kobe had apparently predicted that his niece would arrive on his birthday.

Shaya recalled that Autumn was due on August 21, but Kobe told her that he believed the baby would come two days later.

“She was due August 21st. And when I was pregnant, he was like, ‘Oh, no. She’s coming on my birthday.’ I was like, ‘There ain’t no way.’ ‘Cause that means she’s two days late and she’s getting evicted,” said Shaya .

“There’s no way. And sure as… she came when he was playing in the Olympics in 2008. So while he was playing, I was pushing. Literally. So she was born same birthday.”

Today, that shared birthday has taken on an entirely different meaning for the Bryant family.

Kobe and his 13-year-old daughter, Gianna , were among nine people who died in a helicopter crash in Calabasas, California, on January 26, 2020. The tragedy continues to cast a shadow over significant dates connected to Kobe , particularly his birthday.

The painful reality behind August 23

Shaya explained that grief doesn’t necessarily disappear with time. Instead, important dates can bring those feelings back to the surface.

“It’s just so weird… like I said, when people pass, like our grandparents when they’re older, but with this situation or this happening, it’s more of, it’s like a band-aid, right?” Shaya stated.

“So you think you’re healing and the wound has closed, but then there are anniversaries that come up, birthdays that come up, different things. And it’s such in a public manner that it’s everywhere, like you can’t really heal… nor escape it.”

Kobe’s global fame makes that process even harder. Every August, social media fills with photographs, career highlights, tributes and memories celebrating his life and accomplishments.

While Shaya appreciates the love shown to her brother, she also can’t simply escape the reminders.

She admitted that balancing the two emotions is difficult because she wants her daughter to enjoy her birthday while she’s also grieving and remembering her brother.

The timing is particularly significant because August 24 is recognized as Kobe Bryant Day in Los Angeles and Orange County. The date reflects the two jersey numbers he wore during his 20-season career with the Los Angeles Lakers, No. 8 and No. 24.

Kobe spent his entire NBA career with the Lakers, winning five championships and earning 18 All-Star selections. The franchise retired both of his numbers in 2017, making him the first player in Lakers history to have two numbers retired.

articles.title: LeBron James and Savannah James spend time with children in Akron ahead of his debut with the 76ers
articles.standfirst: James’ latest community effort highlights a legacy that goes far beyond basketball
articles.summary: James’ latest community effort highlights a legacy that goes far beyond basketball
articles.body:
LeBron James may be preparing for the next chapter of his extraordinary NBA career, but his connection to Akron remains as strong as ever.

As the basketball icon gets ready for the new season with the Philadelphia 76ers, he continues to make an impact in the community that has been central to his life and legacy.

James ’ commitment to his hometown was highlighted again as the LeBron James Family Foundation celebrated the ninth anniversary of the I PROMISE School in Akron.

The milestone offered another reminder that, despite his demanding basketball career, James hasn’t lost sight of the young people and families who call his hometown home.

The foundation marked the occasion by sharing images of students returning to school while reflecting on the organization’s journey.

Over the past nine years, the I PROMISE School has grown into more than an educational institution, with its programs designed to support students academically while also helping their families and strengthening the wider Akron community.

The foundation emphasized that its original promise to stand behind students remains unchanged, even as the school and its surrounding programs have evolved.

LeBron’s Akron legacy continues beyond basketball

The I PROMISE School has expanded its approach over the years, incorporating athletics, family support and community-building initiatives alongside education.

Its House system and I PROMISE Athletics program are among the efforts aimed at encouraging accountability, friendship, personal growth and teamwork.

That work represents a particularly personal part of James ’ legacy. Akron is where he grew up and developed into one of basketball’s biggest stars, and he’s repeatedly used his platform to create opportunities for children in the area.

His latest involvement comes at an interesting moment in his career. James stunned basketball fans in July when he revealed that he’d decided to continue playing after initially believing his previous season could have been his last.

He ultimately chose to sign with the 76ers for his record-breaking 24th NBA season.

James explained that his decision wasn’t motivated by money or outside pressure. Instead, he said he still loves basketball, wants to compete and believes he can help Philadelphia challenge for a championship.

While his attention will soon shift toward preparing for his debut with the 76ers, his recent activity in Akron shows that his priorities extend well beyond the court.

The timing has also been a memorable one for James and his family. His wife, Savannah James , recently celebrated her 40th birthday on Aug. 27.

LeBron marked the occasion with a heartfelt social media tribute, calling Savannah his “queen” and expressing his love and appreciation for her.

As James begins another chapter in Philadelphia, his connection to Akron isn’t going anywhere. His playing career may eventually come to an end, but the work he and his family have invested in the city could remain one of the most enduring parts of his legacy.

articles.summary: The Warriors are ready to give Curry everything he needs to finish his career at home
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors appear ready to give Stephen Curry something almost every superstar wants at the end of a legendary career: complete control over his future.

Curry becomes eligible for a new extension on August 29, with the maximum deal reportedly worth two years and approximately $136.7 million.

If he accepts it, the agreement would keep him in Golden State through the 2028-29 season and take his total earnings over the next three years to more than $199 million, including his roughly $62.6 million salary for 2026-27.

However, the money may only be part of the Warriors' remarkable proposal. According to ClutchPoints NBA insider Brett Siegel , Golden State is prepared to let Curry decide what kind of contract works best for him.

That could mean taking the maximum, accepting less money to give the franchise greater roster flexibility, or waiting until next summer to become an unrestricted free agent.

The message is clear, as the Warriors don't want to dictate how Curry's final chapter should look.

Curry holds the key to Golden State's future

Keeping Curry is also a complicated basketball decision for Golden State. The 38-year-old remains one of the league's most influential players, but his age and recent injury history make a long-term commitment more complicated than it would've been earlier in his career.

Curry appeared in only 43 games last season after dealing with a knee injury that kept him sidelined for roughly two months. Even so, his importance to the Warriors extends far beyond what he produces on the court.

He has delivered four NBA championships, changed the way basketball is played and become the defining face of the Golden State franchise.

His presence also remains enormously valuable commercially, making the decision to keep him in the Bay Area about much more than salary-cap calculations.

A maximum extension would guarantee Curry's place in Golden State through the latter stages of his career, but it could also make it harder for the Warriors to add another superstar.

The organization has explored major opportunities involving players such as Giannis Antetokounmpo, LeBron James and Jaylen Brown , yet none of those blockbuster moves came to fruition.

That leaves Golden State facing a difficult balancing act. The Warriors want to maximize whatever remains of Curry's championship window while also ensuring they're not left without a path forward once their franchise icon eventually retires.

Still, everything currently points toward Curry finishing his career where it began. General manager Mike Dunleavy has indicated that neither the team nor Curry is considering another destination, while the Warriors reportedly have no intention of trading him.

After everything Curry has given the franchise, Golden State appears prepared to let its greatest player determine how his final chapter should unfold.

articles.title: Shaquille O’Neal’s latest skill? NBA legend is learning Spanish faster than expected
articles.standfirst: The legendary center's post-playing career has been defined by versatility
articles.summary: The legendary center's post-playing career has been defined by versatility
articles.body:
Shaquille O’Neal has built a career out of surprising people. The four-time NBA champion dominated opposing centers during his Hall of Fame basketball career. After retirement, he successfully transitioned into broadcasting, business, entertainment, music, and philanthropy. Few athletes have managed to remain as visible and influential after leaving the court as the larger-than-life superstar known simply as "Shaq."

Now, according to a young professional basketball player from Colombia, O’Neal may be adding another talent to his ever-growing list: speaking Spanish. Michael Martinez, a professional player for Toros del Valle in Colombia and a rising social media personality known as Colombian College Hooper, recently spent time with the NBA legend and came away impressed by O’Neal’s ability to pick up a new language.

A meeting between two basketball worlds

Martinez has built a following by documenting his journey through basketball, sharing the realities of playing professionally overseas with fans from around the globe. Through social media, he has provided a behind-the-scenes look at life as an international player while inspiring young athletes who dream of pursuing basketball beyond the traditional pathways in the United States.

His recent interaction with O’Neal offered followers a glimpse into a different side of the NBA icon. According to Martinez , one of the most surprising takeaways from their time together was how quickly O’Neal seemed to grasp Spanish words and phrases.

It's easy to forget that O’Neal has always been known for more than basketball. Throughout his career, he has demonstrated an unusual curiosity and willingness to explore new interests, whether that meant becoming a recording artist, earning advanced academic degrees, launching successful business ventures, or working as a television analyst.

Shaq's reputation for reinvention

O’Neal's post-playing career has been defined by versatility. While many former athletes remain connected exclusively to their sport, Shaq has consistently expanded his horizons. He has served as a television personality, entrepreneur, DJ, investor, law enforcement supporter, and motivational speaker, among many other roles.

That willingness to embrace new challenges has helped him remain one of the most recognizable sports figures in the world. The prospect of becoming conversational, or even fluent, in Spanish would only broaden his ability to connect with fans internationally.

Basketball's popularity throughout Latin America continues to grow, and O’Neal already enjoys a massive following in countries across the region. Developing Spanish-language skills could create even more opportunities for engagement with those audiences.

articles.title: Stephen Curry arrived at Warriors alone and built his most important team over 17 seasons while becoming an NBA legend
articles.standfirst: At 38, Curry is facing another enormous decision after spending nearly half his life building something much bigger than anyone could have imagined in 2009
articles.summary: At 38, Curry is facing another enormous decision after spending nearly half his life building something much bigger than anyone could have imagined in 2009
articles.body:
S tephen Curry was 21 years old when the Golden State Warriors called his name with the seventh pick of the 2009 NBA Draft. He arrived without a championship, without an MVP award and without any idea that the franchise taking a chance on him would eventually become almost impossible to separate from his name. He wasn't married yet, either.

Seventeen seasons later, Curry has given Golden State four NBA championships, won two MVP awards and become the greatest three-point shooter the league has ever seen. The skinny guard from Davidson became the face of a dynasty and one of the most recognizable athletes in the world. Now, at 38, the Warriors can put another extraordinary number in front of him: a two-year extension worth as much as $136.7 million.

But that only tells half of what Curry built during those 17 seasons

In 2011, two years after the Warriors drafted him, Curry married Ayesha, the girl he had first met as a teenager. A year later, Riley was born. Curry was still three years away from winning his first NBA championship, and the little girl who would eventually steal the show at his press conferences arrived before the basketball world fully understood what her father was about to become.

Then Curry's two teams started growing almost side by side. Ryan was born in July 2015 , just weeks after Curry won his first NBA championship. Canon arrived in 2018, right in the middle of the Warriors dynasty, after Golden State had won its third championship in four seasons. And in May 2024, Caius arrived. By then, Curry had four rings, two MVP awards, a Finals MVP and virtually nothing left to prove on a basketball court.

Golden State made Curry the face of a franchise. At home, he is simply one of six

Riley is 14 now. Ryan is 11. Canon is 8. Caius, the only one who will grow up without remembering the beginning of his father's extraordinary run, is 2. Stephen and Ayesha celebrated their 15th wedding anniversary this summer.

Those ages matter because they show just how much life has happened while Curry was busy making basketball history.

The 21-year-old who arrived at Golden State in 2009 is now a husband and father of four. He has watched his oldest daughter go from sitting on his lap at press conferences to becoming a teenager. His children have watched him win championships, break records, suffer injuries, come home from road trips and get up to do it all over again.

And Curry doesn't talk about that part of his life as something secondary to basketball. Earlier this year, he called raising four children with Ayesha “beautiful chaos.” Watching four different personalities develop, he said, has been the “best gift and responsibility” of their lives.

The Warriors can offer Curry $136.7 million and the possibility of playing through age 40. For Golden State, the decision could shape the final years of the greatest player in franchise history. For Curry, those same years will also happen while Riley becomes a young woman, Ryan moves deeper into her teenage years, Canon continues growing up and little Caius begins forming the childhood memories he may one day have of his father still playing in the NBA.

None of that means Curry is ready to walk away. Basketball remains part of who he is, and he has spoken about the court still being his happy place. But at 38, time looks different than it did at 21.

When Curry arrived in 2009, Golden State gave him a jersey and a place to begin his NBA career. Over the next 17 seasons, he helped turn that team into a dynasty.

Away from the arena, he and Ayesha were building another one.

And now, as one team decides how much it is willing to give Stephen Curry for the next two years, the other one is already waiting for him at home.

articles.title: Ja Morant returns to his old high school with daughter in his arms to see permanent tribute inside gym
articles.summary: Ja Morant returned to the place where his basketball journey began, and this time he wasn't alone.
articles.body:
Ja Morant returned to the place where his basketball journey began, and this time he wasn't alone.

The NBA star walked into Crestwood High School in Sumter, South Carolina, smiling and greeting people with his 7-year-old daughter Kaari in his arms as the school unveiled a permanent insignia inside the gym honoring his journey from Sumter to the NBA.

It's a very different scene from Morant's days as a teenager walking through the same school. He left Crestwood as its all-time leading scorer with 1,679 points before eventually becoming an NBA superstar.

The homecoming also gave something back to the next generation. Nike and Hibbett awarded $50,000 to Crestwood's boys and girls basketball programs as Morant returned to the gym where his own story started.

articles.title: Victor Wembanyama’s summer transformation has NBA fans convinced a revenge tour is coming
articles.standfirst: The Spurs franchise cornerstone spent the offseason focused on adding strength
articles.summary: The Spurs franchise cornerstone spent the offseason focused on adding strength
articles.body:
V ictor Wembanyama was already one of the most terrifying players in basketball. Now, according to a growing number of fans on social media, he might be even bigger.

Photos and videos of the San Antonio Spurs superstar during France's recent international games have sent the basketball world into a frenzy, with many observers convinced that Wemby added significant muscle over the summer.

Some fans have even speculated that the 22-year-old may have grown taller, with reports and online discussions suggesting the French phenom could now stand around 7-foot-6 or taller. One thing is clear: Wembanyama looks noticeably different. And NBA fans have already started imagining what that could mean for the rest of the league.

The arms everyone is talking about

The biggest talking point isn't Wembanyama's height. It's his biceps. For years, critics pointed to the French star's slender frame as one of the few weaknesses in his game. Opposing teams often tried to counter his skill and length by attacking him physically in the paint. That strategy may become much harder this season.

Recent images have showcased a visibly stronger Wemby, with fans immediately noticing increased muscle definition in his arms and shoulders. Social media platforms were flooded with reactions comparing his current physique to previous seasons, with many concluding that the Spurs franchise cornerstone spent the offseason focused on adding strength.

For a player who already possesses elite shot-blocking instincts, perimeter skills, and unprecedented reach, additional strength could make him even more difficult to defend, and even more difficult to move.

The "French Alien" looks ready

The timing of the transformation has only fueled excitement. Wembanyama is coming off a season that ended in heartbreak after the Spurs fell to the New York Knicks in the NBA Finals . While reaching the championship series represented a major milestone for San Antonio's rebuilding project, the loss left Wembanyama one step short of capturing the first NBA title of his career.

Fans have not forgotten. Judging by the reaction online, many believe the disappointment may have created an even more dangerous version of the player known as the "French Alien." Every new photo, highlight, or international performance has generated the same type of comments: Wembanyama looks stronger, taller, and motivated. And that's a frightening combination for the rest of the NBA.

The scary part isn't simply the physical transformation. It's what happens when that transformation is combined with Wembanyama's existing skill set. Even before this offseason, he was already one of basketball's most unique talents. Standing well over seven feet tall with guard-like ball handling, shooting ability, and defensive versatility, Wembanyama has consistently done things that should not be possible for someone his size.

He is widely regarded as one of the game's premier young stars and one of the most physically gifted players in NBA history. If he has truly added meaningful strength while maintaining his mobility and coordination, opposing defenses could face an even bigger challenge.
